summary: Your Hindi videos do far better on Instagram than YouTube. Instagram gets 1,200-1,400 views on the best ones, while YouTube mostly gets under 50. The winners are robots and 'weird behavior' explanations (a robot falling without a gyro, a clap switch that only hears noise, a tiny mic acting like a speaker). Generic 'how does X work' videos about everyday places (lift, mall door, tap, smoke alarm) get weak results, and the single English video got no Instagram views at all.
winningPattern: Short Hindi videos about a robot or a surprising sensor trick, with a curious or contrarian title such as 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' or 'without X the robot fails'. The topic is a hands-on maker item (gyro, clap switch, line follower, mic, PIR). Instagram is the main driver, and the best ones also earn saves and likes. The title is short, uses simple Hinglish and often has one emoji.
doMore: Make robot and maker-project videos that show a clear failure or surprise (what happens without the part).
Use the 'it doesn't do X, it only does Y' title format, as in Clap Switch and Mic.
Post Hindi first on Instagram, then repost to YouTube with a stronger first-second hook.
Aim for saveable content: simple one-idea explainers that students will want to revisit.
Keep the topic set to Arduino-style parts (gyro, IR, PIR, mic, line sensors) and test one new variation per week.
stopDoing: Stop making near-duplicate videos on the same topic (two IR, two smoke, two tap videos split the audience).
Stop generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on public-place gadgets like lifts, mall doors and street lights.
Stop English uploads for now, since there is no sign of an audience for them yet.
